players.product: EMD Electronics: specialty gases / precursors, patterning materials and CMP slurries

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Helene von Roeder: Q2 2026 group net sales rose to EUR 5.434 billion from EUR 5.255 billion, with organic growth of 4.1% (CEO Kai Beckmann), EBITDA pre up to EUR 1.6 billion from EUR 1.46 billion (organic +9.3%, margin 29.4%) and EPS pre up 6.9% to EUR 2.16. Life Science grew 8% organically (Process Solutions +15%, Advanced Solutions +4%, Discovery Solutions +2%) with EBITDA pre of EUR 700 million at a 29% margin; Healthcare sales rose 2.4% to EUR 2.2 billion but fell 3.4% organically; Electronics grew 11.7% organically to EUR 871 million of sales after the Surface Solutions divestment. Operating cash flow was EUR 605 million and net financial debt EUR 9.2 billion at June 30.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 2026 net sales EUR 5.434 billion; organic growth 4.1%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Kai Beckmann: Merck raised its 2026 guidance to organic sales growth of 1%-3% (from 0%-3%), net sales of around EUR 21 billion-EUR 21.8 billion, EBITDA pre of EUR 5.9 billion-EUR 6.3 billion (from EUR 5.7 billion-EUR 6.1 billion) and EPS pre of EUR 7.90-EUR 8.60. Electronics: organic sales growth 6%-9% (from 3%-7%) and EBITDA pre of around EUR 1 billion (organic growth 25%-29%); Life Science: organic sales growth 5%-7%, including a potential tariff-refund headwind of around EUR 40 million, and EBITDA pre of EUR 2.6 billion-EUR 2.8 billion; Healthcare: organic sales -4% to -2%, assuming zero US Mavenclad sales from August, and EBITDA pre of EUR 2.8 billion-EUR 3 billion. CEO: 2027 should be well in line with the organic projections of the 2025 Capital Markets Day.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 EBITDA pre EUR 5.9 billion-EUR 6.3 billion; EPS pre EUR 7.90-EUR 8.60

quarterly_data.signal: Electronics CEO Benjamin Hein: Semiconductor Solutions grew 17% organically in Q2, driven by AI-related applications in advanced nodes in both logic and memory; semiconductor materials (around 65% of Electronics sales) grew at a low double-digit rate, after averaging low-teens growth over the past 10 quarters, and Delivery Systems & Services (less than 15% of sales) was helped by finishing a large project, with H2 expected roughly flat versus H2 last year. Optronics was largely flat; CFO Helene von Roeder: it faces softer consumer-electronics demand influenced by high memory prices, which could result in a year-on-year sales decline in H2, and Electronics EBITDA pre was EUR 244 million at a 28% margin, about 200 basis points above Q1's underlying margin. Hein: Electronics EBITDA pre was up 87.5% organically, helped by the Surface Solutions divestment, volume leverage, cost management and a positive AI-driven mix.
quarterly_data.figure: Semiconductor Solutions +17% organic; Electronics EBITDA pre margin 28%

quarterly_data.signal: Electronics CEO Benjamin Hein: the leading-edge customers behind the AI-driven growth remain capacity constrained into the second half and well into 2027; 'there is a shortage of memory chips', prices for advanced memory chips are very high, and Merck expects this to continue at least until the second half of 2027 while it works with customers on debottlenecking.

CEO Kai Beckmann: in June Merck opened a new metrology and inspection site near Grenoble, France, a EUR 20 million investment that expands its capacity for M&I tools; Electronics CEO Benjamin Hein: metrology and inspection is a relatively small business whose integration is going extremely well, and it matters more as advanced packaging tightens quality requirements.
quarterly_data.figure: EUR 20 million Grenoble metrology and inspection site

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Kai Beckmann: Merck signed a definitive agreement on June 25 to acquire Bio-Techne's operations (reagents, analytical instruments and precision-medicine diagnostic systems); CFO Helene von Roeder: closing is expected by the end of 2026 or in early 2027, with run-rate cost synergies of approximately EUR 140 million by year three. CEO: if closed as planned, it would add close to 5% to group sales growth and about 10% to Life Science, and be immediately accretive to the group EBITDA pre margin.
quarterly_data.figure: run-rate cost synergies approximately EUR 140 million by year three

quarterly_data.signal: Life Science CEO Jean-Charles Wirth: Process Solutions grew 15% organically in Q2 on healthy market demand, the new go-to-market model, special buying by a very few Asian customers linked to the Middle East conflict, exceptional China growth from customers ordering equipment for new plants and non-repeat integrated-workflow orders; full-year Process Solutions growth should land in the upper range of 8%-12%, H1 book-to-bill was above 1 and should stay above one, no destocking is expected in 2026 (any may come in 2027), and 75%-80% of orders carry lead times of one to six months. The largest customer is less than 1%-2% of revenue in any Life Science unit; the Blarney, Cork site is ramping and a new bioprocessing site in Daejeon, South Korea opens in October.

players.product: oncology and immunology drug-discovery programs with Recursion's AI-driven design platform (healthcare business)

quarterly_data.signal: Healthcare CEO Danny Bar-Zohar: the first patient was dosed in the phase III trial of Merck's first-in-class anti-CEACAM5 ADC in third-line metastatic colorectal cancer, which Merck decided to develop on its own rather than partner; the FDA granted breakthrough therapy designation to enpatoran for lupus with active cutaneous manifestations; the FDA accepted the full BLA for Pergoveris, though 'considerable uncertainty' remains about approval; atacicept, approved for IgA nephropathy, leaves Merck a net royalty upside in the single-digit % range plus milestones; Pimicotinib had first sales in China with US launch preparations underway (CEO Kai Beckmann).

Healthcare (CFO Helene von Roeder): EBITDA pre was EUR 747 million at a 34.7% margin; the rare-disease products delivered combined H1 sales of EUR 207 million; Specialty Care declined 6% organically on Mavenclad's loss of US market exclusivity, while Erbitux grew 5%. Healthcare CEO Danny Bar-Zohar: US Mavenclad sales were almost on par with Q1 but weakening, with two generics approved and two more possibly entering in Q3; Mavenclad grew 32% in Europe in Q2, and European exclusivity is expected to end in August 2027. Pergoveris grew 14% in Q2, sold over EUR 300 million year to date, is approved in 116 countries including China, and fertility and endocrinology improved from -5% in Q1 to -1% in Q2.
quarterly_data.figure: Healthcare EBITDA pre EUR 747 million (34.7% margin)
